phase_name: Regression cases pinning the ordering invariant

objectives.description: test-please-grant.sh: /tag-shaped mint in committed-events.jsonl fixture leaves tree clean
Confirm each new case actually fails against pre-Phase-2 behavior

notes: Re-ran both suites against an isolated copy of push-grant-lib.sh reverted to the pre-Phase-2 (Phase-1-only) commit content. Result: 3 of 5 new cases correctly FAIL against that pre-fix state -- the two clean-tree-pin cases (/tag mint in test-please-grant.sh; wrapper push in test-guard-git-push.sh) and the buffer-not-log companion case -- confirming they genuinely pin the ordering regression. The remaining 2 (revoke-then-flush audit-guarantee; flush-idempotence) pass under both old and new code by design: they exercise pg_audit_buffer/pg_audit_flush's OWN correctness (added in Phase 1, unaffected by Phase 2's mint/consume rewiring), not the ordering bug itself, so a pre-Phase-2 pass is expected and not a test-quality defect. All 5 pass against the current (post-Phase-4) codebase; only the pre-existing, unrelated 'expired grant' failure (recorded in Phase 1) remains in test-guard-git-push.sh.
